_about: Built by files/pirate-ship/economy/build-economy-data.py from skill-tree.json and GOODS.md. Do not edit by hand. Marks: source = a period record (GOODS.md Part 4); proposed = this session's placement for Rex; unsourced = Rex's design addition with no period source; estimate = worked out from sourced inputs (GOODS.md 1j). basePrice is null everywhere: the balance lane sets it; the sourced price text is beside it. The five per-settlement numbers (stock, consumption per day, target reserve, production per day, base price) belong to a ports file that does not exist yet (ALIGNMENT §10).
note: An occupation is a label, not a skill: it groups the skills a person of that calling practised, levels nothing, grants nothing, and a character may carry more than one (Rex, 2026-10-28). The words are the ones period wills and indentures use; the record styles a person by ONE word, and a second appears for a small minority (under 5% of mariners), nearly always sea + shipboard craft: 'Mariner and Cooper', 'Mariner and Surgeon'. 'Alchemist' was never an occupation (0 wills; 'Chymist' 40): use Chymist. Status words (Gentleman, Yeoman, Captain) sat in the same slot as trades. Grey chips are STATS.md skills with no goods tree. Source: research-occupations.md. Metal trades: six London companies back the split (research-metal-trades.md); whitesmith found no evidence and is not a skill; locksmith, farrier, nailer and anchorsmith fold into Blacksmithing on Campbell's word. Medical trades: Campbell's five 'Professors' back the split; bonesetter, tooth-drawer and quack were empirics, not trades, and fold into Surgery's tiers; Black healers and obeah are in the secondary literature only (open).
rules: one word per character by default; the word of their highest skill group
a second word for a few: sea + craft ('Mariner and Cooper'), or 'Merchant, Commander'; 'Barber-Chirurgeon' is one compound trade
status words are not occupations: Gentleman, Esquire, Yeoman, Husbandman, Captain/Colonel (militia), Servant, Labourer; they can sit beside a trade word
no bonus from the label itself; any synergy comes from the skills (Rex: later, if at all)

occupations.name: Planter
occupations.period: trade-cum-status; 'Planter of Saint James, Barbados' (1670)
occupations.note: The sugar planter's works: fields, boiling house, still-house (L). Boiler and distiller as job titles: open for 1657

occupations.name: Husbandman
occupations.period: status of a small farmer, used as a trade in indentures (1654–86)
occupations.note: Rex's 'Agriculturalist'. Yeoman is the richer man, same work

occupations.name: Hunter (boucanier)
occupations.period: Exquemelin: Hispaniola's three callings, 'hunt, plant, pirate' (1684)
occupations.note: the boucan is Preserving

occupations.name: Fisherman / Turtler
occupations.period: turtlers in sloops at the Caymans (D)
occupations.note: salt-rakers and pearl-divers fall here; no will title found for either (open)

occupations.name: Woodcutter (logwood-cutter, collier)
occupations.period: the Campeche cutters (D); collier for charcoal
occupations.note: no will title found; the cutters were 'Jamaica men' by origin, not trade (open)

occupations.name: Miner / Refiner
occupations.period: off-map in this period (Spanish silver, European iron)
occupations.note: a label the Caribbean town will rarely use

occupations.name: Victualler / Cook
occupations.period: 'Victualler' (Bristol 1694; Spalding 1642); the ship's Cook among the exempted tradesmen (Smith 1627)
occupations.note: Rex's 'Food Artisan'. Miller, Baker and Butcher were each a trade of their own in a town; a small port lumps them

occupations.name: Chandler
occupations.period: 'Tallow chandler' (Spalding 1642)
occupations.note: the INFP's calling; wax figures are a design extension

occupations.name: Tanner / Currier
occupations.period: 'Tanners, Curriors, Shoemakers' at Port Royal 1688 (Taylor)
occupations.note: the currier dressed the tanned hide; folded into Tanning here

occupations.name: Cordwainer
occupations.period: 'Cordwainer' (Spalding 1642; indentures); 'Shoemakers' at Port Royal 1688

occupations.name: Sugar-baker
occupations.period: 'Sugar Baker' (Exeter 1661), 'Sugar Refiner' (London 1694)
occupations.note: in England the refiner; on the island the boiler. One label for both

occupations.name: Distiller
occupations.period: 'Distiller' (London 1692; Distillers' Company 1638)

occupations.name: Dyer
occupations.period: a London company trade; no Caribbean will title found (open)
occupations.note: indigo-making on the plantation was planter's work under an overseer (D)

occupations.name: Perfumer
occupations.period: no period Caribbean source (Rex's addition)
occupations.note: unsourced

occupations.name: Chymist
occupations.period: 'Chymist' (Southwark 1728), 'Chemist and Apothecary' (1729); never 'Alchymist'
occupations.note: Rex's 'Alchemist' group, under its period name. Campbell: 'The Chymists are generally Apothecaries'

occupations.name: Powder-maker
occupations.period: powder mills in England; no Caribbean mill in the sources

occupations.name: Blacksmith (anchorsmith, farrier, locksmith)
occupations.period: 'Blacksmith' (Port Royal 1692); Blacksmiths' Co. 1571; Campbell: anchor-smith a branch, locksmith 'see Smith', Farriers' Co. 1674
occupations.note: Rex's 'Metalworker', the common kind. Ligon's plantation had a 'Smiths forge'

occupations.name: Gunsmith (armourer)
occupations.period: Gunmakers' Co. 1637; 'gun and sword smiths' at Port Royal; 'Mariner and Armourer' (will); Campbell: armourer 'merely nominal' by 1747
occupations.note: the ship's armourer repairs; the gunsmith makes

occupations.name: Cutler (sword-cutler)
occupations.period: Cutlers' Co. 1416; Campbell separates cutler from sword-cutler; Hounslow and Shotley Bridge sword works (1630, 1691)

occupations.name: Founder (gunfounder, pewterer, brazier)
occupations.period: Founders' Co. 1614; King's Gunfounder 1615; Pewterers' Co. by 1348; Armourers merged with Brasiers 1708
occupations.note: all off-map until a foundry exists in the game's Caribbean

occupations.name: Goldsmith (silversmith)
occupations.period: 'Goldsmith of Jamaica' (1693); Goldsmiths' Co.; silversmiths at Port Royal

occupations.name: Carpenter (joiner, sawyer)
occupations.period: 'Carpenter' (Port Royal 1707), 'Joiner' (1723); Campbell: the joiner 'generally the same Person with the Carpenter'
occupations.note: Rex's 'Woodworker', the common kind

occupations.name: Cooper (hooper, turner)
occupations.period: 'Cooper' (Nevis 1705); 'Mariner and Cooper' (8 wills 1669–1725); 'Hooper' (Bristol)
occupations.note: the commonest sea + craft pairing; 'the common Turner is generally a Cooper' (Campbell)

occupations.name: Shipwright (boat-builder, caulker, block-maker)
occupations.period: 'Shipwright' (Stepney 1699); 'Mariner and Shipwright' (4 wills); 'Mariner and Caulker' (3); Shipwrights' Co. 1605/1612
occupations.note: Bermuda's cedar sloops; the Boston yards

occupations.name: Cabinetmaker (carver)
occupations.period: Campbell 1747 entries; 'Cabanittmakers' at Port Royal 1688 (second-hand)

occupations.name: Millwright (wheelwright)
occupations.period: Campbell 1747 entries; Ligon asked for 'Mill-wrights, Wheel-wrights' (1657)
occupations.note: the sugar island's indispensable man

occupations.name: Weaver / Spinster
occupations.period: weaver by-employments at Spalding 1642; 'Spinster' is a status word for an unmarried woman in wills, from the trade
occupations.note: Rex's 'Textile Artisan', first half

occupations.name: Ropemaker
occupations.period: 'Ropemakers' at Port Royal 1688 (Taylor)

occupations.name: Taylor
occupations.period: 'Taylor' (Antigua 1707); 'Taylors, Hatters' at Port Royal 1688

occupations.name: Sailmaker
occupations.period: 'Petty, as Sail-maker' at the Cape Coast trial (J); indenture trade
occupations.note: the ship's tradesman; needle and palm

occupations.name: Chirurgeon (barber-chirurgeon, surgeon's mate)
occupations.period: 'Chirurgeon' (Barbados 1675); 'Barber Chirurgeon' (306 wills 1660–1730); 'Mariner and Surgeon' (1706)
occupations.note: a craft, bound seven years and examined by the Company; the ship's and the pirates' surgeon. The ISFJ doctor's calling

occupations.name: Apothecary
occupations.period: 'Apothecary' (Jamaica-bound 1702)
occupations.note: Society of Apothecaries 1617; could prescribe after the Rose case (1703/04). Ligon's plantation 'Doctor'. The INTJ's calling

occupations.name: Physician (Doctor in Physic)
occupations.period: 'Doctor in Physic' (Port Royal 1725); College of Physicians 1518; Campbell's first 'Professor' of the medical trades
occupations.note: a learned status as much as a trade; rare in the colonies

occupations.name: Druggist
occupations.period: Campbell 1747: 'to buy up, in large Quantities, all manner of uncompounded Drugs'; a weekly printed bill gave drug prices
occupations.note: a merchant of drugs, not a maker; the shopkeeping kind

occupations.name: Midwife
occupations.period: licensed by the diocesan bishop, c. 1500–18th c.; an 'unofficial apprenticeship' (Evenden)
occupations.note: a licensed calling with no skill of its own here: the game has no childbirth system (open for Rex)

occupations.name: Mariner
occupations.period: the catch-all sea word in wills ('Mariner of Port Royal', 1683); Smith 1627 splits Sailers (able) from Younkers (foremast men)
occupations.note: Master and Mate are ranks inside it, not occupations

occupations.name: Gunner
occupations.period: 'Mariner and Gunner' (1667); Gunner among the ship's officers (Smith 1627)
occupations.note: fires the guns; does not make the powder unless he also has that skill

occupations.name: Soldier (marine, militia)
occupations.period: militia ranks 'Captain', 'Colonel' are status; the boarders in Roberts' articles
occupations.note: Rex's 'Military Specialist'. Combat classes are a later topic

occupations.name: Merchant / Factor
occupations.period: the commonest Port Royal will word (19 of 100); 'Merchant, Commander' (1684)
occupations.note: Rex's 'Merchant / Diplomat'. Grocer, Vintner, Linen-draper, Ironmonger are the shopkeeping kinds

occupations.name: Musician
occupations.period: 'served as Musick' at the Cape Coast trial (J); musician by-employment at Spalding
occupations.note: usually a second word: three of Spalding's four musicians had another trade

occupations.name: Gamester / Sharper
occupations.period: no will title (nobody wrote 'gamester' on a will); a reputation, not a trade
occupations.note: the den's people
